Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed October 5, 2026, 2:30 AM ET / 06:30 UTC (Revision 3)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The branch moves persisted-turn replay validation into existing transcript readers and makes internal prompt admission awaitable while preserving synchronous agent entry. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** This remains a useful, distinct performance improvement. The reviewed source and recorded boundary proof reveal no blocking correctness or security defect. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `d14e903971c4e06f45840790fb467b04efa3c7c2` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | The focused implementation has strong paired measurements and boundary coverage, with no actionable introduced finding. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The recorded isolated workload exercises the changed replay owner with real SQLite workers and shows all six replay caller cohorts at zero MAIN statements on the pinned candidate. Production-worker fault cases cover rewrite, database closure, run revocation, and identical-file replacement before consumption; prompt/core cases cover permission replacement and disposal. No stored-data contract changes, so migration proof is not applicable. This review inspected source and recorded evidence without executing tests. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The recorded isolated workload exercises the changed replay owner with real SQLite workers and shows all six replay caller cohorts at zero MAIN statements on the pinned candidate. Production-worker fault cases cover rewrite, database closure, run revocation, and identical-file replacement before consumption; prompt/core cases cover permission replacement and disposal. No stored-data contract changes, so migration proof is not applicable. This review inspected source and recorded evidence without executing tests. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Pinned introduced changes: Reviewed the merge-base-to-head production hunks separately from base-branch drift. Replay preparation retains physical source identity, validates writer and context facts through the anchor reader, and consumes once within its callback.
Final-effect authority checks: The reader retains writer FIFO custody and checks physical identity, current reader ownership, and the native mutation revision before consumption. Prompt admission then checks permission generation and session preparation identity before committing prompt state and entering the agent loop.
Production-worker refusal coverage: The introduced regressions delay an actual worker response, then rewrite the transcript, close the database, or revoke the run; each requires rejection before consumption. A separate case replaces the physical database with identical bytes. Permission and core-loop cases check rejection before prompt publication or model requests. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Replay admission lets an interrupted agent resume an already-persisted user turn without appending it again. It checks session ownership and transcript state before publishing the prompt and starting model execution. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Interrupted user turn] --> B[Prepare transcript replay] B --> C[Retain original database] C --> D[Reader validates writer and version] D --> E[Recheck permissions and run authority] E --> F[Consume replay once] F --> G[Start agent synchronously] G --> H[Settle outside reader custody] ``` ## Before merge None.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Not applicable as a bug reproduction: the performance claim has a pinned paired workload, and current-main source confirms synchronous replay checks remain. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Extending the existing reader snapshot and retaining its admission custody is a focused solution that preserves the established writer and prompt owners.
